```markdown
# Roadmap — SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). One uv workspace holding the four packages under `packages/` (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a chosen quarter range, downloaded once as a baseline | §3 R1; §2.1; §4.2 | A | 1 | Requests are trivial: one master.idx plus listings per quarter at 3 req/s (§4.8). Bytes, rows, time and memory per quarter are measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | Daily filing indexes added on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs | §3 R2; §4.2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year, one per business day, plus listings. Per-file size is measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | A canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet, built from the downloaded indexes | §3 R3; §4.4; §4.6 | A | 3 | Compute (elapsed time, peak memory) measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The ingestion running on Azure: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Azure Monitor | §3 R4; §4.1; §4.9 | A | 4 | Azure spend is unknown until deployed and is measured by the Stage 8 smoke run (§7 step 4). Your partner's time: ADR acceptance and deployment settings (§7 step 1) |
| O5 | Backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation sharing one downloader, parser and publisher | §3 R5; §4.1 | A | 5 | Not material beyond O1–O3 |
| O6 | Reprocessing from stored original bytes, with no new download | §3 R6; §4.3; §4.5 | A | 6 | Retained raw bytes ≈ O1 volume plus each changed snapshot. Measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | Periodic re-reading of quarterly indexes, with additions and changes accounted for | §3 R7; §4.2; §4.4 | A | 7 | Each weekly run re-downloads every supported quarter, so about the O1 baseline volume each week (§4.8) |
| O8 | One shared SEC request budget, however many workers run | §3 R8; §4.3 | A | 8 | Not material |
| O9 | Readers find the current dataset through one versioned pointer per quarter | §3 R9; §4.5; §4.6 | A | 9 | One generation per quarter per change. Storage depends on the retention policy |
| O10 | Records leave the catalog only through explicit approval tied to a source hash | §3 R10; §4.4 | A | 10 | Your partner's time: one approval per gated closed-quarter candidate. The frequency is unknown until reconciliation runs on real data |
| O11 | Stated defaults held in reviewed configuration and validated before any network request | §3 R11; §4.8; §5 | A | 11 | Not material |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

Order follows your ranking except in three places, each for a dependency or information reason:

- **O3 joins O1 in Stage 1.** A baseline nobody can read gives no usable result.
- **O4 (Azure) moves to Stage 8.** The core runs locally on real data first, and the platform deploys a worker that already exists.
- **O11 lands just before Azure.** Its keys span every earlier stage.

- [ ] Stage 1: Local quarterly baseline slice
      Objective: Download one real archived quarter with an identifying, throttled client, keep its original bytes, and parse it into canonical rows in Parquet.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing (generated package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a quarterly collector and parser producing `sec-index-v1` rows from retained raw bytes; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one real archived quarter's master.idx stored with its SHA-256, byte count and source URL. O3 — a Parquet file of `sec-index-v1` rows whose count reconciles with the source's data lines, with malformed rows refused rather than dropped. The findings file records measured bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory and request count for the real run.
      Leaves out: daily ingestion and shared commands (Stage 2); source manifest and processing states (Stage 3); versioned publication (Stage 4); shared request lease (Stage 5); reconciliation (Stage 6); full configuration validation (Stage 7); Azure deployment (Stage 8); golden-fixture validation suite, observability and alerts, runbooks, scheduled triggers (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily ingestion through shared commands
      Objective: Discover and ingest every listed daily index from a handoff date, through the same discover/collect/transform commands as the quarterly baseline.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1's collector, parser and findings
      Produces: the `sec-edgar-ingest` discover, collect and transform commands with quarterly and daily source selection; deduplication of baseline/daily overlap
      Exit: O2 — from a real handoff date, every listed daily index through the present is ingested, across a quarter boundary, and an immediate rerun reports `no_new_sources`. O5 — quarterly and daily sources pass through identical download, parse and transform code, differing only in source selection.
      Leaves out: source manifest and processing states (Stage 3); versioned publication (Stage 4); shared request lease (Stage 5); golden-fixture validation suite (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Source manifest and replay
      Objective: Record source, snapshot, workset-binding, processing and attempt identities so that any stored input reprocesses without SEC access.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stage 2's shared commands
      Produces: source manifest and processing states (`downloaded -> transformed -> published`), immutable worksets, and a replay path that reads raw storage only
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds observations from retained raw bytes with zero SEC requests. Unchanged hashes and versions skip the work, and a partially completed workset resumes without redoing finished members.
      Leaves out: Azure Table Storage backing (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each affected quarter as a complete generation behind a conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 3's source manifest and processing states
      Produces: versioned publication (generations, manifest.json, changes.parquet, conditional active pointer) and the reader contract
      Exit: O9 — readers that resolve the pointer see only complete generations under injected crashes before files finish, before the pointer update and after it. A competing publisher cannot overwrite a newer pointer.
      Leaves out: withdrawal gate (Stage 6); Azure Table Storage backing (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Shared SEC request budget
      Objective: Put every SEC request, including discovery and retries, behind one renewable lease and one rate target.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stage 2's shared commands
      Produces: shared request lease, bounded retry policy, and the halt on access denial
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors issue requests from one holder at a time at or below the configured rate, with retries counted. Lease loss stops requests, and a 403 halts the run.
      Leaves out: Azure Storage-backed lease (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and gated withdrawals
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, apply safe changes, and hold closed-quarter removals for approval bound to a hash.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 4's versioned publication; Stage 5's shared request lease
      Produces: the reconciliation command, change reports, the withdrawal gate and approval records
      Exit: O7 — a real reconciliation run records additions and field updates as a new generation and leaves unchanged quarters untouched. O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval names its exact source hash. Open-quarter absence and stale daily replay remove nothing.
      Leaves out: Azure deployment (Stage 8); runbooks (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Configuration and stated defaults
      Objective: Move every stated default into typed, reviewed configuration that is validated before any external I/O.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stages 1–6's commands and their settings
      Produces: full configuration validation (`conf/sec-edgar-ingest.yaml`) and the configuration error outcomes
      Exit: O11 — each Configuration refusal listed in §5 exits with its named error before any network request, and the §4.8 starting values load from a single reviewed file.
      Leaves out: environment-specific deployment values (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 8: Azure deployment
      Objective: Run the shared worker on the Azure platform in an isolated environment, with production triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stage 7's full configuration validation; ADR and spec accepted (§7 step 1)
      Produces: Azure deployment (infrastructure as code, managed identities, ADF pipelines, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS and Table Storage backing, Azure Storage-backed lease) and a pinned image digest
      Exit: O4 — in an isolated environment, the integration tests pass against real identities, job start/poll, the Storage lease and conditional pointer updates. A live smoke run of one archived quarter and one daily index records bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, request rate and Azure cost (§7 step 4), and replays from raw storage with SEC access disabled.
      Leaves out: observability and alerts, runbooks, scheduled triggers (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 9: Production baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Harden for production, run the real backfill and catch-up, and enable the daily and weekly triggers.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7 (production standard)
      Consumes: Stage 8's Azure deployment
      Produces: golden-fixture validation suite, observability and alerts, runbooks, scheduled triggers, and a release record
      Exit: O1 — every requested baseline quarter is published, or the incomplete range is explicitly approved and recorded. O2 — the daily trigger is enabled after an accepted catch-up, and observed scheduled runs have durable reports. O7 — one manual reconciliation runs with its gated candidates resolved, then the weekly trigger is enabled and observed.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked:

1. Re-run the gap rubric over O1–O11, with evidence per verdict: the implementing stage and plan, any Deviation notes, and any deferred_items entries.
2. List as unmet each numbered spec requirement (R1–R11) that no outcome's `Spec` cell cites.
3. Each unmet item exits as a new stage or as a deferral with a written reason.
```
